title: Northwind Advisory 'Our Team' headshot rescue: neutralise six differently-lit staff portraits to one card-calibrated house look by eye, retouch, and deliver matched colour + clean B&W crops
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Freelancer.com brief titled "Traditional Corporate Headshot Session Needed" (classic/formal corporate head-shots, neutral light-grey backdrop, colour + clean black-and-white versions, deliverables for social-profile/company website/print, one-week turnaround). All names and the firm are FICTIONAL and invented for this benchmark: "Northwind Advisory Partners" is a made-up boutique wealth-advisory firm with invented staff (Adaeze Okonkwo, Julian Hartmann, Mei-Lin Castellano, Rafael Ibarra, Priyanka Deshmukh, Tomas Bergqvist) and an invented office manager (Priya Venkataraman); no real company, person, or trademark is referenced. The original post asks a photographer to also SHOOT the session, which is out of connector scope, so the task is faithfully scoped to the POST-PRODUCTION deliverable a headshot retoucher actually hands over once the captures exist. It is ENRICHED past the shallow original in the one way real 'Our Team' refresh jobs actually get hard: instead of one tidy same-lighting session, the firm supplies SIX staff portraits accumulated over months in different rooms and lighting (cool strobe, window-warm/tungsten, green office-fluorescent, under- and over-exposed, flat-neutral), each with an 18% neutral grey reference card visible at the frame edge, and the whole point is to normalise all six to ONE house look. The retoucher neutralises each card BY EYE (the connector has no eyedropper/ruler) and reports the per-frame settings it dialed; the numeric neutralisation/brightness tolerance is the grader's acceptance check on the delivered files, not a step the agent performs. The real-world intent (formal corporate headshots, colour + clean B&W, social-profile/site/print use, a consistent look across the set) is preserved exactly; nothing is invented beyond what a matched-gallery job requires.
one_line_ask: Take six staff headshots shot under deliberately mismatched lighting — each with an in-frame neutral grey card — and grade every one BY EYE to a single house look (neutralise each card, match the set's brightness), then tastefully retouch, convert clean neutral black-and-white alternates, and deliver the matched colour + B&W crops with the grey card cropped out, reporting the final per-frame white-balance and exposure parameters you applied.
full_brief:
Hi, this is Priya Venkataraman, office manager at Northwind Advisory Partners (a boutique wealth-advisory firm). We're rebuilding our 'Our Team' web page and we have a mess to clean up. Over the past year, six of our people sat for head-shots, but they were taken at different times in different rooms by whoever was around, so the set does NOT hang together: some are warm and orange from window light, one's got a horrible green office-fluorescent cast, a couple are too dark or too bright, and one was shot under a cool studio strobe. They look like six different companies. Please work only from the files I'm attaching: six high-res portraits of six staff members against our neutral light-grey seamless, plus a one-page house-standards brief. You'll notice each photo has a small neutral grey calibration card clipped at the edge of the frame — the photographer left those in on purpose so whoever finished them could get the colour right.

What 'done' means for us:
1. Make the six read as ONE consistent set. Use the grey cards as your eye reference: work each finished image until its card looks genuinely neutral (no colour tint left in it) and until the whole set sits at one shared brightness, so the portraits share one white balance and one tonal look. This is the whole job — if the set still looks like it was shot on six different days, it's not done. Please note that the six were lit differently, so you can NOT push the same correction across all of them; each one needs its own fix to land on the same target.
2. Give the set an intentional, premium studio finish — clean contrast, natural warm-neutral skin, nothing flat and nothing garish. Traditional and formal, not trendy.
3. Tasteful, believable retouching only: gently brighten each person's eyes and teeth, and even out the light on the face. No plastic skin, no reshaping, no touching the light-grey backdrop.
4. For every finished colour portrait, also give us a clean, true black-and-white version — a neutral monochrome finish, not a heavy filter.
5. The grey cards are just calibration aids — they must NOT appear in anything you deliver. Crop them out; every delivered portrait is subject-only.
6. Crops: everyone gets the website 'Our Team' portrait at 4:5 1600x2000 (colour and B&W). Our two founding partners, Adaeze Okonkwo and Julian Hartmann, also need a 1:1 square social-profile/avatar crop (1200x1200) and a 5:7 print crop (1500x2100) for framing at reception, in colour.
6b. When you hand it over, tell us exactly what you did to each frame — the white-balance and exposure settings you landed on per person — so we can see they were actually matched to the same target and not just eyeballed carelessly.

Turnaround within the week. Deliverable: a consistent, print/web-ready 'Our Team' headshot package (matched colour + clean B&W, cards removed) with a short note of the final per-frame settings you applied.

connector_workflow.note: Upload the six differently-lit staff portraits plus the house-standards brief into the working project so the grade chain runs against real asset references. Plumbing, not difficulty.
Level Adaeze's ~2-degree tilt before any tonal work.

Authored grade of the COOL-STROBE frame, BY EYE: dial temperature warmer (with a small tint) until the blue-reading grey card looks genuinely neutral, set exposure so the frame reaches the intended house brightness, and build contrast/clarity while holding whites below clipping for the premium house look. Reason the warm amount FROM this frame's blue cast — it is NOT reused on the others. This frame's landing point anchors the shared look the rest are matched to. Authored grade of the WARM window/tungsten frame, BY EYE: dial temperature COOLER — the opposite sign to Adaeze — until the orange-reading card looks neutral, and pull exposure slightly to bring this brighter frame down to the set's shared brightness; match contrast/clarity to the house look. Applying Adaeze's warming here would deepen the orange — which is exactly why a single shared correction cannot serve both. REPORT the move. acceptance (grader-checked): on the RETAINED pre-crop master (julian_retouched) the grey-card region reads neutral within ~3 levels and brightness matched to the set; card-exclusion is checked separately on the delivered crops.

TRIAGE grade of the FLUORESCENT frame, BY EYE: the cast is GREEN — a TINT problem, not a blue/orange temperature problem — so the dominant move is a magenta TINT shift (image_apply_adjustments tint) until the green card and the skin look neutral; a small temperature trim; then contrast/clarity to the house look. A temperature-only correction like the other frames would leave a green card and sickly skin — the failure this frame is designed to expose. REPORT the tint/temperature/exposure you dialed. acceptance (grader-checked): on the RETAINED pre-crop master (castellano_retouched) the grey-card region shows no residual green (within ~3 levels) at the set's brightness; card-exclusion is checked separately on the delivered crops.

Grade of the UNDEREXPOSED frame, BY EYE: raise exposure and lift shadows/blacks (protecting texture, not crushing) until the dark grey card rises to sit at the set's shared brightness, then a WB trim to neutralise. Exposure moves UP here — the opposite of Priyanka's frame — so a shared exposure value cannot serve both. REPORT the move. acceptance (grader-checked): on the RETAINED pre-crop master (ibarra_retouched) the grey-card region reads neutral (within ~3 levels) and brightness matched to the set; card-exclusion is checked separately on the delivered crops.

Grade of the OVEREXPOSED frame, BY EYE: LOWER exposure and recover highlights/whites until the washed card comes down to the set's shared brightness without greying the skin, restore contrast, and cool the slightly warm card to neutral. Exposure moves DOWN — the mirror of Rafael. REPORT the move. acceptance (grader-checked): on the RETAINED pre-crop master (deshmukh_retouched) the grey-card region reads neutral (within ~3 levels), skin not greyed, brightness matched to the set; card-exclusion is checked separately on the delivered crops.

Grade of the FLAT near-neutral frame, BY EYE: its card already looks close to neutral, so the work is TONAL — add contrast and clarity and set the black point to reach the house look from a hazy original, with only a minor WB trim. chaining_note: Strict output-to-input chaining throughout, and difficulty is deliberately NOT sourced from the crops. Step 1 loads the six frames + the standards brief (the agent reads the brief for the acceptance intent it grades toward BY EYE; it never inspects a pixel). Steps 2-13 pair a straighten with ONE authored image_apply_adjustments grade per frame, each carrying a DIFFERENT reasoned correction toward a single shared look, judged by eye against the in-frame grey card: Adaeze warms (blue card), Julian cools (orange card, opposite sign), Mei-Lin gets a magenta TINT (green card, a different axis than temperature), Rafael lifts exposure (dark card), Priyanka pulls exposure/recovers highlights (bright card, opposite sign to Rafael), Tomas builds contrast/blacks (flat but near-neutral card). The agent REPORTS the final per-frame temperature/tint/exposure it dialed; the grader (which can measure) checks the RETAINED pre-crop masters' grey cards against the neutrality tolerance, while card-exclusion is checked separately on the delivered crops (which have the card removed). Steps 14-25 run the selective eyes/teeth retouch on each colour master (select_by_prompt then a masked image_apply_adjustments consuming base-image + mask; masks are supported on image_apply_adjustments, not on image_adjust_light_portions). Steps 26-31 author a clean neutral B&W of each master via image_apply_adjustments (saturation -100 + tonal response). Steps 32-47 fan each finished master to its crops with the grey card excluded: six colour 4:5 (32-37), six B&W 4:5 (38-43), and the two founding partners' extra 1:1 and 5:7 colour crops (44-47). Every mask/edit/crop consumes only prior named outputs; the only input-less root is the legitimate upload. The 16 delivered files emerge purely from the chain, and the reasoning load sits in the six divergent grades and the triage, not in the crop count.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon multi-asset EDIT whose hardness is craft, not step count: 47 connector calls, 5 distinct Adobe tools, but the difficulty is concentrated in a cross-asset colour-consistency problem judged against an in-frame reference. Six portraits shot under genuinely different light (cool strobe, warm window/tungsten, green fluorescent, under- and over-exposed, flat-neutral) must all be neutralised BY EYE to ONE house look using each frame's 18% grey card as the visible target. Because the six start from different casts and exposures, the corrections DIVERGE in both sign and kind — warm vs cool, exposure up vs down, and one frame needs a green-magenta TINT correction rather than a blue-orange temperature move — so any naive one-recipe-for-all pass (or per-frame image_apply_auto_tone, which optimises each frame independently and cannot converge them on a shared look) visibly fails to match the set. hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (a craft decision with a visible failure mode, not a self-measured loop): the agent must apply a DIFFERENT correct correction to each frame — warming the blue cool-strobe card, cooling the orange window card, a magenta TINT (not a temperature move) on the green fluorescent card, exposure UP on the dark frame, exposure DOWN on the washed frame, and pure tonal work on the flat near-neutral frame — all converging BY EYE on one shared house look, and REPORT the per-frame WB/exposure it dialed. The naive path (one warming recipe across all six, or per-frame image_apply_auto_tone) looks plausible and visibly breaks the set: the green frame stays green and sickly, the cool and warm cards diverge, and the flat frame stays hazy. Getting the wrong correction is a decision the agent can trip, and it is visible in the delivered images (and to the grader who measures the cards). HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: (1) cross-asset consistency to a shared reference — six differently-lit portraits neutralised to one card-calibrated look, each needing its own delta of a different sign (warm vs cool) and even a different kind (a green-magenta TINT vs blue-orange temperature); (2) triage of superficially similar inputs — the 'cool-looking' blue-strobe frame and the green-fluorescent frame demand opposite axes (temperature vs tint), and the flat-but-near-neutral frame looks 'done' yet needs the most tonal work, so the wrong choice is invisible until the set is seen side by side; plus disciplined selective eyes/teeth retouch via a masked image_apply_adjustments lift (masks are supported on image_apply_adjustments, not on image_adjust_light_portions), never a global brighten, and an authored neutral B&W (desaturate + tonal response, not a canned filter). TRAP: pushing one warming/auto-tone recipe across all six converges nothing; a secondary trap is treating the flat frame's already-neutral card as 'finished'; a third is leaving the calibration grey card in the delivered crop. MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION (grader-checked on the output, never read by the agent), stated as TWO decoupled claims so it is never self-contradictory: (a) neutralisation is graded on the RETAINED pre-crop master of each frame (adaeze/julian/castellano/ibarra/deshmukh/bergqvist_retouched, card still in frame) — its grey-card region reads neutral (R/G/B within ~3 levels of spread) at the set's shared mid-tone brightness; (b) card-exclusion is a SEPARATE check on each delivered crop — the card is fully cropped OUT (subject-only, no card pixels), the neutrality tolerance never being evaluated on a cropped file. Plus exact crop pixels (4:5 1600x2000 for all six colour + B&W; 1:1 1200x1200 and 5:7 1500x2100 for the two partners, ~300 DPI print intent), sRGB, plus the agent's reported table of the final per-frame WB/exposure parameters it applied.
